title: Batching operational notes - first responders weekly
content:
Overview:
This is the weekly operational digest for the 'first responders' rotation focused on batching, kernel sandbox experiments, and KV cache shadowing. Intended audience: oncall, kernel owners, and anyone iterating on throughput/latency tradeoffs. Rough, frequently edited.

This week highlights:
- Rolled a lightweight batching throttle to 10% of traffic in eu-west for two days (benefit: tail latency dropped ~18% for short requests).
- Reproduced the KV shadow warmup regression seen in canary (root cause appears to be a scheduling gap when a prefill and an eviction coincide).
- Kernel sandbox: micro-preempt handshake tweak merged to feature branch; still flaky under thermal throttling.

Standup log snippets (daily):
2028-01-03 09:15 - Quick triage: evening throttles left persistent queues; restarted prefill coordinator on two hosts. Diego observed memory spike after kernel handshake.
2028-01-04 10:00 - Maya: rolled back kernel-scheduler tuning on node pool beta-3 after jitter. Priya: started a shadow run for sticky-prefix cache config.
2028-01-05 11:20 - Ethan: validated batch-throttle telemetry shows the fastlane path is being used by ~12% of requests (expected 10-15%).

Incidents / Triage notes:
- Incident INF-4187 (2028-01-04 02:30 UTC): High 95th latency in eu-west for <64-token requests. Cause: batch window extension interacting with a long-running KV eviction job. Mitigation: temporary reduction of window to 8ms and isolated eviction to maintenance pool. Follow-ups: introduce eviction backoff when active batching above 60% occupancy.
- Near-miss - kernel handshake times out under thermal load on p4d-4x nodes. Repro steps in sandbox: replay synthetic burst with seq_len=64, concurrent=110. Outcome: handshake timeouts ~1.2% of requests, triggers fallback route.

Kernel sandbox experiments (notes):
- Experiment: 'preempt-window-fence'
  - Hypothesis: adding a lightweight fence around preemptible kernel switches reduces mid-batch stalls by preventing concurrent eviction of handshake resources.
  - Setup: sandbox cluster t-sandbox-6, 8k synthetic requests over 30m, mixed seq lengths.
  - Results: 5% reduction in batch stall rate, but CPU context switch increased by ~2%.
  - Open: measure latency impact under real traffic distribution.
- Experiment: 'microkernel-handshake-retries'
  - Added jittered retry (backoff up to 6ms) for initial handshake. Cut handshake timeouts by ~60% in sandbox but introduced occasional burst latency spikes.

KV cache shadowing and behavior:
- Observed: warmup regression on canary when shadow cache load > 120% of main cache RPS. Symptoms: warmup misses cascade into slower first-token latencies.
- Hypothesis: our shadow prefill thrashing with eviction algorithm (LRU hysteresis) causes oscillation.
- Short-term patch: cap shadow prefill concurrency per host (PR linked). Deployed to canary; monitoring for TTL skew.
- Sticky-prefix proposal (notes to self): for token prefixes seen > threshold, pin them in an L1 sticky set for 10s to improve repeat short sessions. Need to model memory overhead.

Batching and throttle playbook (operational):
- Fastlane (first-responder) behavior:
  - Eligibility: requests under 48 tokens, no function calls, route flagged as latency-critical.
  - Path: immediate microbatch (<4 requests) using preempt window=6ms; otherwise fall back to normal batching.
- When to reduce throttle: if 95th tail increases > 15% compared to baseline for 10m AND SLO error budget consumed > 3%.
- Emergency steps:
  1) Flip throttle to 0% for region.
  2) Add temporary capacity (burst pool) or route to older-but-stable kernel variant.
  3) If KV eviction correlated, isolate eviction to maintenance nodegroup.

Metrics snapshot (control plane numbers):
- Baseline avg latency (short): 42ms -> after throttle test: 35ms avg, 95th 120ms -> 98ms.
- Batch occupancy: normal 8.9 -> test 7.4.
- Shadow cache prefill success: 82% -> dropped to 68% during canary regression.

Action items (owner - due):
- Diego - add eviction backoff when batch occupancy > 60% (2028-01-16)
- Priya - run sticky-prefix memory model + simulation and share cost estimate (2028-01-13)
- Maya - extend kernel sandbox telemetry to include thermal/CPU counters for 72h (2028-01-12)
- Ethan - ops doc: step-by-step rollback play for fastlane throttle (2028-01-11)
- Hannah - triage INF-4187 postmortem draft (2028-01-14)

Notes to self / loose ideas:
- Could we adaptively shrink prefill sizes when we detect eviction storms? Would need a short feedback loop from node-level eviction metrics into prefill coordinator.
- Consider an A/B test for sticky-prefix only for sessions that have > 3 sequential requests in 10s.
- Explore a cheap Bloom-filter based warmup filter for shadow cache to avoid prefill storms.

Meeting attendees (weekly sync 2028-01-06):
- Ethan (owner), Priya, Maya, Diego, Hannah, + SRE oncall (Liam), product (Anjali - perf priorities).
Key decisions from meeting:
- Keep fastlane throttle experiment running in eu-west for one more week; extend telemetry capture.
- Do NOT enable sticky-prefix globally until memory model validated.

Unresolved questions / blockers:
- Thermal-triggered kernel handshake timeouts: hardware vs kernel preemption policy? Need vendor input (NVIDIA support ticket opened).
- Shadow warmup regressions sometimes correlate to GC cycles in host process; is host GC scheduling amplifying effect? Need to reproduce with host GC disabled in sandbox.

Appendix - quick links and commands:
- Reproduce batch stall locally: ./scripts/replay_workload --seq=64 --concurrency=110 --duration=300 --target=t-sandbox-6
- Fastlane throttle toggle: infra-toggle fastlane eu-west --percent=0/10/100
- Relevant PRs: PR #824 (shadow prefill cap), PR #832 (microkernel handshake jitter)

If anything is missing or you want raw traces, ping me in #serving-runtime or drop into the oncall channel.

-- Ethan  (notes will evolve)
